scope: Insurance/TPA CDM & preventive programme admin (3d) + ID-vs-MY readiness compare

medium_claims.claim_text: Malaysia NHMS 2023: only 34.4% of tracked DM patients achieved HbA1c ≤6.5% target; mean HbA1c 7.7% nationally.
medium_claims.rationale: Two independent primary-academic sources corroborating the same metric; neither is a government statistics agency or multilateral, so High threshold not met.

medium_claims.claim_text: Malaysia NDR 2023: only 34.4% of DM patients achieved HbA1c ≤6.5% target.
medium_claims.rationale: Same two independent primary-academic sources as PP6.1-C5; repeated citation of the same verified figure in PP6.2 context.

override_triggers.description: Claims explicitly tagged [ASSUMED-N] are auto-Low regardless of supporting sources
Claims about vendor's own product/capability/size sourced from that vendor's own marketing pages or press releases
Market sizing sourced solely from NextMSC, Faber Consulting, Ken Research — private aggregators with no primary-tier cross-validation
Operating cost figures, frequency metrics, or regulatory claims sourced only from trade publications, news wire, or secondary commentary — no primary-tier source
Claims evidenced by exactly one source, regardless of source quality tier
Claims appearing in the ID-vs-MY readiness matrix without a numbered footnote traceable to a source in Stage 6 artifacts

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Only 32% of 273 assessed FKTPs met Level 4 RPPT (controlled CDM patient ratio) by December 2023; FKTPs achieving Level 4 receive full KBK capitation, those below receive reduced payments.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Single primary-ministry source. The BPJS JKN journal is an official publication but lacks corroboration from an independent source. The RPPT figure is the central frequency/severity metric for PP6.1 and is cited four times across the two artifacts. A second independent source confirming the 32% Level 4 rate and KBK structure would raise this to Medium.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search for: (1) BPJS Kesehatan Annual Report 2023 PDF (laporan tahunan) for PROLANIS RPPT national statistics — URL pattern: bpjs-kesehatan.go.id/laporan-tahunan; (2) WHO/P4H PROLANIS programme evaluation documents citing RPPT performance data; (3) peer-reviewed assessment of KBK capitation outcomes post-2022 in PubMed/PMC. Specific query: 'PROLANIS RPPT Level 4 controlled rate 2023 site:bpjs-kesehatan.go.id OR site:pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov'

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: PROLANIS biannual HbA1c examinations documented as 'not being carried out' at multiple FKTPs due to supply and staff capacity constraints.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Single secondary-trade source (Pharmacognosy Journal). This claim is the structural failure mode underpinning PP6.1's argument that monitoring breaks down at the lab-result collection stage. Without primary-tier corroboration, the claim rests on a single journal article of unclear peer-review status. The same scoping review (PMC12538241) is available and covers PROLANIS barriers — check whether it directly cites the HbA1c gap, which would provide a primary-academic co-citation.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Fetch full text of PMC12538241 (PROLANIS 2025 scoping review, already cited at PP6.1-(8)) to check whether it explicitly documents HbA1c examination non-completion as a barrier — if yes, this gives a primary-academic second source at zero additional fetch cost. Also search: 'PROLANIS HbA1c pemeriksaan tidak dilaksanakan site:pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov OR site:bpjs-kesehatan.go.id'; additionally search BPJS Kesehatan monitoring reports (DM program evaluations, laporan kinerja) for HbA1c completion rates.

weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Malaysia PDPA Amendment Act 2024 (effective January 1, 2025) adds mandatory breach notification; health data remains sensitive personal data under Section 4; employer-TPA CDM data flows without updated consent language may create breach exposure.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: Two secondary-trade law firm commentary articles only. The PDPA compliance tension is a root cause in both PP6.2 and PP6.3 and underpins the regulatory positioning of the entire Malaysia CDM analytics opportunity. A direct citation from the Malaysian Attorney General's Chambers official gazette, the PDPC (Personal Data Protection Commissioner) official guidance, or Parlimen Malaysia published Act text would provide a primary-ministry source and raise this to Medium. The Baker McKenzie article is closer to authoritative but is still secondary commentary, not the official text.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Fetch the Malaysia Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 official text from: (1) Attorney General's Chambers Malaysia — agc.gov.my (search for 'Personal Data Protection Amendment Act 2024'); (2) PDPC Malaysia official guidance page — pdp.gov.my; (3) Parlimen Malaysia official act text. Specific query: 'Personal Data Protection Amendment Act 2024 Malaysia site:agc.gov.my OR site:pdp.gov.my'. Confirm Section 4 sensitive personal data definition and the breach notification timeline that is now effective.

gate_reasoning: Stage 6 scores 0% High, 4.4% Medium, and 95.6% Low across 45 scored claims. The two Medium scores are a repeated citation of the same Malaysia NDR/NHMS DM control figure. Every cost estimate, labor-time estimate, and willingness-to-pay figure is tagged [ASSUMED-N] and auto-Low. The central PROLANIS performance metric (32% Level 4 RPPT) is a single primary-ministry source with no corroboration. Nine distinct vendor-marketing citations (Naluri CDMP page, PMCare homepage, AIA Vitality factsheet, BP Healthcare POPE page) are used to evidence claims about those same vendors' products and member counts — all auto-Low under the vendor-marketing override. Market sizing rests entirely on NextMSC, Faber Consulting, and Ken Research (all aggregator auto-downgrades). The ID-vs-MY readiness matrix contains three claims with no numbered citations traceable within Stage 6 artifacts. Deep research is warranted on at least the three identified weak claims before Stage 6 can support a credible gate-pass; the two High-priority targets (RPPT corroboration via BPJS annual report and PROLANIS HbA1c gap via PMC12538241 full-text check) are low-cost fetches that could meaningfully improve score distribution if successful.
